anomalies.description: A mounted knight on a brown horse rears up aggressively toward another knight on a dark horse, initiating a physical confrontation; the horses are close and the posture suggests imminent or ongoing combat.

Two knights on horseback engage in direct combat: one raises a mace-like weapon and swings it downward toward the other, who is seated and appears to be bracing or reacting; the motion and proximity confirm active melee fighting.
A mounted knight in full armor with a lance engages in combat with a warrior (William Wallace) on horseback wielding a sword; the sequence shows charging, clashing, and pursuit across an open field.

Two mounted warriors engage in a high-speed cavalry duel: one (William Wallace) wields a sword, the other (a knight in white surcoat and helmet) wields a lance; they charge, clash, and the knight is struck and thrown from his horse.
A mounted warrior is violently thrown from his horse during a combat maneuver; the motion blur and body position indicate a forceful dismount likely caused by an opponent's strike or evasive action.
The fallen knight lies on the ground while the victor (Wallace) rides away; the knight’s weapon (sword) is seen embedded in the ground near him, indicating the conclusion of the combat.
A fallen warrior lies prone on the ground while a sword is thrust downward into his back, indicating a deliberate attack on a helpless victim.
A knight in armor repeatedly strikes a prone, helpless man lying on the ground with his armored fist or gauntlet.

A man with long hair (William Wallace) engages in close-quarters combat with a knight, grabbing the knight’s helmet and pulling him down, then subduing him on the ground while holding a sword to his throat.

After subduing the knight, the attacker holds the knight’s head and presses a blade against his neck while the knight is clearly helpless and screaming; this constitutes abuse of a defenseless victim.

The victim, now subdued and looking upward with wide eyes and open mouth, remains under control of the attacker who holds their head and a blade near their neck—indicating continued domination of a helpless person after initial combat.
